text:
Alex (CS): Heads-up — new customer (FinHealth) onboarding hit a regress: their integrator SDK goes into a retry/backoff loop and never surfaces the real quota error to the app. They see retries every ~2s, then long exponential backoffs, then eventual 429s. Renewal check-in is tomorrow, so this is time-sensitive.
Maria (Eng): Can you paste the logs? Which SDK version?
Alex (CS): SDK v0.9.2 (js). App logs show repeated attempts: 
```
2025-06-25T14:03:12Z request start /v1/generate
2025-06-25T14:03:12Z response 429 {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":null}
2025-06-25T14:03:14Z retry attempt 1
2025-06-25T14:03:16Z response 429 {"error":"rate_limit_minute","retry_after":10}
```
Alex (CS): Note: SDK resolves 429 into a transparent retry loop (internal backoff) and doesn't return the 429 up to the integrator, so their app never shows an error and they think requests hang.
Sam (Onboarding): Customer said they started with load testing earlier today, maybe hit per-minute quota, then did a quick restart. Could be they exceeded minute-level token quota accidentally.
Julie (Support): Is this the same behavior as the old 429->non-propagation bug we saw in v0.9.0? I thought we patched that.
Maria (Eng): We patched a path for streaming endpoints but I don't think the non-stream codepath was updated. Looks like SDK treats all 429s as transient and retries without bubble-up. That's risky for customers doing synchronous calls.
Alex (CS): Customer expects a 4xx surfaced so they can show an error page and stop hammering. Right now they hit renewal risk because product looks flaky.
Maria (Eng): Quick triage plan: 1) Can you grab full request/response headers (esp X-RateLimit-* and x-request-id)? 2) We can push a small SDK patch to expose a config flag to disable auto-retry. 3) Add short-term Console tweak to surface minute-window 429 counts per API key.
Alex (CS): Sending headers now. Also they reported the SDK's default retry backoff grows to >1m which blocks their worker.
ops-bot: Incident opened — CS-2025-489 "SDK auto-retry hides 429 during onboarding" by Alex (CS). Priority: P2.
Julie (Support): I uploaded the headers to the ticket: x-ratelimit-limit-minute=60, x-ratelimit-remaining-minute=0, x-ratelimit-reset-minute=18, x-request-id=req_9a8b7
Maria (Eng): Thanks. That confirms minute quota hit. We'll do a hotfix: expose option `autoRetry: false` and make SDK surface 429 with code `RATE_LIMIT_MINUTE`. I'll PR to v0.9.3 patch branch now.
Sam (Onboarding): Meanwhile I'll ask the customer to throttle to 10rps and enable client-side backoff. Also sending them a config snippet for the SDK: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: "...", autoRetry: false, onError: err => console.log(err.code, err.message) })
```
Alex (CS): Customer is happy to try that. Can we also add a temporary Console alert for this org so their engineers see minute-window usage spikes?
Maria (Eng): Ops: can we add an org-level alert? @ops-bot
ops-bot: Alert rule created for org finhealth-org: "minute_quota_spike" threshold=50% within 5m.
deploy-bot: CI green for sdk/js v0.9.3-patch, deploying to canary.
Maria (Eng): Canary deployed. Patch exposes 429 to callers and returns structured code RATE_LIMIT_MINUTE. Also added telemetry event so Console can show per-key minute resets.
Sam (Onboarding): Customer confirmed test with autoRetry:false — they saw the 429 surfaced and were able to reduce their send rate. App no longer appears hung.
Alex (CS): Great. I'll run renewal prep: note fix, include ask to adopt 0.9.3 and the opt-out flag, plus a doc blurb for onboards re: minute quotas.
Julie (Support): Capturing feedback: update onboarding checklist to include load-test supervision and ensuring SDK >=0.9.3 before stress tests. Also filing a docs PR.
Maria (Eng): Follow-ups: (1) Add an integration test to ensure 429s are surfaced for non-stream endpoints, (2) consider defaulting autoRetry:false for server-side SDKs.
Alex (CS): Thanks team. I'll mark ticket CS-2025-489 as "mitigated — patch deployed, customer validated" and leave for post-mortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
